prompt:
You maintain a running summary of a long engineering document that is being read part by part, so that a later reader can model the system in SysML v2 without seeing the earlier parts.
Update the summary with the new part. Keep, as compactly as possible: the full names of system elements, actors and items; every alias or call sign with the full name it stands for; which element produces, sends or receives which item; modes and normative requirements. At most 300 words.

Current summary:
System: Cedar Falls Municipal Drinking Water Treatment Plant control system; boundary River Intake Pump Station/Raw Water Screen Channel to High Service Pump Header. Aliases: Ironwood=River Intake Pump Station (start permissives; lost permissive→alarm/stop; maintenance release after logged isolations). Lantern=SCADA Historian Server (critical; trends/doses/analyzers/filters/washes/lab times; uses Sample Chain Slip; retention; test time sync/tag naming/retrieval). Marigold=Coagulant Dosing Skid (sends Alum Batch Ticket; receives Jar Test Photograph Set; holds last approved dose on bad data). Cobalt=North Filter Gallery (staggers washes). Sparrow=Laboratory Sample Receiving Bench (sends Jar Test Photograph Set). Quarry=Maintenance Planner (receives Clearwell Diver Entry Permit, Rake Torque Snapshot, Pump Bearing Vibration Clip vs inspection intervals; reviews accounts, commissioning defects, nuisance alarms, drift before PM intervals). Juniper=High Service Pump Header (produces Pump Bearing Vibration Clip; lead/lag; demo stable pressure startup/transfer/shutdown). Falcon=Distribution Dispatcher (sends Pressure Zone Handoff Card→South Distribution Pressure Station; confirms readiness acknowledged before zone changes; notified of pressure failures). Elements: Raw Water Screen Channel (Rake Torque Snapshot); South Filter Gallery (Filter Run Exception Note→Chief Operator); Clearwell Level Controller (sends Clearwell Diver Entry Permit); Chlorine Contact Basin; Backwash Recovery Tank; North/South Distribution Pressure Stations (comms loss→last mode; readiness checks); backup generator, ATS, UPS. Actors: Chief Operator (sends Backwash Solids Manifest→Residuals Hauler; alarm governance; training; post-event review), Duty Engineer (receives Chlorine Cylinder Seal Log; authorizes bounded workarounds), Laboratory Technician (Sample Chain Slip; no control actions; trained), Chemical Supplier Driver (Chlorine Cylinder Seal Log), Residuals Hauler, Field crews. Item: Chlorine Residual Alarm (high priority; test annunciation/ack/escalation). Mode: Storm Intake Mode (planned drill). Requirements: RBAC, no shared credentials, least privilege, MFA remote access, segmentation, tested patches; alarm priority by consequence; controlled shelving; backup power for key loads; UPS bridges transfer; sensor-failure detection; functional/integrated commissioning tests before distribution; distribution readiness only after pressure, clearwell, comms, contacts verified; operator training.

New part:
S246: The Chemical Supplier Driver shall follow site access, unloading, verification, and communication procedures established during commissioning and confirmed during training.
S247: Records generated during commissioning and early operation shall be complete enough to support troubleshooting, regulatory review, warranty claims, and future operator training.
S248: Records retention shall follow municipal policy and applicable drinking water requirements, with electronic records protected against unauthorized change and accidental loss.
S249: Periodic performance reviews shall compare actual plant operation with the control concept, including alarm burden, manual interventions, water quality stability, chemical use, and energy use.
S250: Continuous improvement actions shall be prioritized by risk, reviewed by the Chief Operator and Duty Engineer, tested before release, and incorporated into updated procedures and training materials.

Return JSON {"summary": "..."}.
